name: Vancouver
blurb: Ski, climb and kayak on the same spring day: the North Shore peaks rise straight out of the city's backyard.

name: Victoria
blurb: BC's capital sits at the southern tip of Vancouver Island, gazing across the strait at the Olympics.

name: Whistler
blurb: Host of the 2010 Olympic alpine events and jumping-off point for the Spearhead and Fitzsimmons traverses.

name: Stanley Park
blurb: A 400-hectare forested peninsula ringed by the Seawall, bigger than Central Park in NYC.

name: Kelowna
blurb: Okanagan wine-and-beach city on the shore of Okanagan Lake, supposed home of the lake monster Ogopogo.

name: Mt Robson
blurb: At 3,954 m it's the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies, and its summit is famously shrouded in cloud most days.

name: Whitehorse
blurb: Yukon's capital on the Yukon River, once the head of sternwheeler navigation for Klondike stampeders.

name: Kamloops
blurb: Sagebrush and hoodoo country where the North and South Thompson rivers meet.

name: Nanaimo
blurb: Harbour city on Vancouver Island's east coast, and namesake of the famous no-bake bar.

name: Prince George
blurb: Northern BC's hub at the confluence of the Fraser and Nechako rivers.

name: Okanagan Lake
blurb: A 135 km long glacial trench lake stretching from Vernon to Penticton.

name: Grouse Mountain
blurb: Home of the Grouse Grind, a 2.9 km stair-master of a trail gaining about 850 m.

name: Penticton
blurb: Squeezed between Okanagan and Skaha lakes, with world-class gneiss cragging just south of town.

name: Fraser River
blurb: BC's longest river rises near Mt Robson, loops north to Prince George, then carves the Fraser Canyon to the sea.

name: Squamish
blurb: The Outdoor Recreation Capital of Canada: granite big walls, kiteboarding, mountain biking and bald eagles.

name: The Chief
blurb: The Stawamus Chief is a 700 m granite monolith; the Grand Wall is one of Canada's most iconic rock climbs.

name: Garibaldi Lake
blurb: Its startling turquoise water is held back by The Barrier, a lava dam of unstable volcanic rock.

name: Joffre Lakes
blurb: Three glacier-fed lakes stacked beneath Matier Glacier, just off the Duffey Lake Road.

name: Tofino
blurb: Surf town at the end of Hwy 4 on Vancouver Island's wild west coast, gateway to Clayoquot Sound.

name: Revelstoke
blurb: Powder town between the Selkirks and Monashees, with the most vertical of any lift-served resort in North America.

name: Golden
blurb: Where the Kicking Horse meets the Columbia; a base for the Rockies, Purcells and Rogers Pass.

name: Sea-to-Sky Hwy
blurb: Highway 99 climbs from Howe Sound past the Chief and Brandywine Falls to Whistler and Pemberton.

name: Bugaboos
blurb: Granite spires jutting from Purcell glaciers; Conrad Kain climbed Bugaboo Spire in 1916 and called it his hardest ascent.

name: Mt Garibaldi
blurb: A heavily eroded stratovolcano whose rubbly Atwell Peak dominates the view north from Squamish.

name: Haida Gwaii
blurb: An archipelago of about 150 islands off the north coast, sometimes called the Galápagos of Canada.

name: Dawson City
blurb: Heart of the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush, sitting where the Klondike River joins the Yukon.

name: Kluane Lake
blurb: Yukon's largest lake, beside the Alaska Highway at the edge of Kluane National Park.

name: Nelson
blurb: Heritage mountain town on Kootenay Lake's West Arm, home to Whitewater's deep powder.

name: Pemberton
blurb: Seed-potato farming valley under Mt Currie's 1,700 m north face, at the start of the Duffey Lake Road.

name: Fernie
blurb: Coal-mining town turned ski mecca in the Lizard Range, famed for its deep powder storm cycles.

name: Coquihalla Hwy
blurb: Highway 5 from Hope to Kamloops, star of Highway Thru Hell; the summit near Zopkios is a classic ski tour.

name: Mt Waddington
blurb: At 4,019 m the highest peak entirely in BC, a rime-plastered tower guarded by huge glaciers.

name: Wedge Mountain
blurb: At 2,892 m the highest summit in Garibaldi Park, reached via the Wedgemount Lake hut.

name: Sky Pilot
blurb: A craggy 2,031 m summit looming over the Sea to Sky Gondola, above Howe Sound.

name: Mt Slesse
blurb: Its knife-edged NE Buttress is a North American classic; a 1956 airliner crash site lies on its slopes.

name: Spearhead Traverse
blurb: A horseshoe ski traverse from Blackcomb to Whistler over a dozen glaciers, often done in a single long day.

name: Howser Towers
blurb: The Bugaboos' highest summit; the Beckey-Chouinard on South Howser Tower is one of the Fifty Classic Climbs.

name: Rogers Pass
blurb: The railway's 1880s route through the Selkirks, now a legendary ski touring zone with a permit system.

name: Mt Sir Donald
blurb: Its Northwest Ridge offers roughly 1,000 m of quartzite scrambling, a Rogers Pass rite of passage.

name: Mt Begbie
blurb: A glaciated 2,733 m peak that forms Revelstoke's skyline, south of town across the Columbia.

name: Mt Joffre
blurb: Highest peak of the Joffre Group; its north couloir is a coveted steep ski line.

name: Tantalus Range
blurb: A jagged glaciated wall across the Squamish River from Hwy 99; crossings start with a river boat or a fixed rope.

name: Bella Coola
blurb: Tidewater village at the end of Hwy 20 and 'The Hill,' ringed by heli-ski terrain in the Coast Range.

name: The Lions
blurb: Twin granite summits above Howe Sound; the Squamish people call them the Twin Sisters.

name: Skeena River
blurb: BC's second-longest river flows through the Coast Mountains past Terrace to tidewater near Prince Rupert.

name: Skaha Bluffs
blurb: Hundreds of sunny gneiss sport routes above Skaha Lake, a spring and fall escape from coastal rain.

name: Duffey Lake Rd
blurb: Highway 99 from Mount Currie to Lillooet; Cayoosh Pass at the top has endless ski touring right off the road.

name: Lake O'Hara
blurb: A Yoho gem reachable by a limited-seat bus or a long walk; Abbot Pass hut sat above it until 2022.

name: Mt Assiniboine
blurb: The Matterhorn of the Rockies straddles the Divide; its summit lies on the BC side in Mt Assiniboine Park.

name: Golden Hinde
blurb: At 2,195 m it's Vancouver Island's highest peak, deep in the backcountry of Strathcona Park.

name: Cape Scott
blurb: The storm-lashed northwest tip of Vancouver Island, end of the North Coast Trail.

name: Chilkoot Trail
blurb: The 1898 stampeders' route over Chilkoot Pass; the Canadian half drops past Lindeman Lake to Bennett.

name: Takakkaw Falls
blurb: Fed by the Daly Glacier, it drops about 373 m in Yoho; the name comes from a Cree word for magnificent.

name: Mt Logan
blurb: Canada's highest peak at 5,959 m, with perhaps the largest base circumference of any mountain on Earth.

name: Tombstone Park
blurb: Jagged granite peaks along the Dempster Highway, dubbed the Patagonia of the North.

name: Miles Canyon
blurb: Basalt-walled gorge on the Yukon River just upstream of Whitehorse that wrecked many stampeders' boats.

name: Carcross Desert
blurb: Sand dunes left by an ancient glacial lake bed, often billed as one of the world's smallest deserts.

name: Yukon River
blurb: The Klondike highway of 1898: paddlers still float it from Whitehorse to Dawson on a ~715 km journey.
